extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, and scholars of literature and film
extracted.subtask_short: analyzing duras's literary and film style
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and evaluate characteristic qualities, techniques, and themes in Marguerite Duras's writing and films, as described in the Wikipedia article. Useful for close reading, literary/film analysis, or preparing secondary-source overviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of prose / importance of what is unsaid
rubrics_metrics.description: With Moderato Cantabile, she became more experimental, paring down her texts to give ever-increasing importance to what was not said.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate Duras by how she uses omission and minimal language to create tension and subtext; strong examples include Moderato Cantabile and other mid-career novels. Anti-patterns: over-explication or reductive summary that ignores silences/ellipses in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command of dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: She was noted for her command of dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the strength and function of spoken exchanges—how dialogue carries subtext, shapes character, and creates rhythmic or theatrical effects. Check plays and novels (e.g., her theatrical works and dialogues in novels) for exemplary usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental form / association with the nouveau roman
rubrics_metrics.description: She was associated with the nouveau roman French literary movement, although she did not belong definitively to any one group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge work by formal experimentation (structure, point of view, narrative conventions). Note hybridity: Duras borrows avant-garde techniques without full allegiance to a single movement. Examples: shift from conventional early novels to experimental later works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filmic technique: divorcing image from sound and symbolic space
rubrics_metrics.description: Her films purposely lacked realistic representation, such as divorcing image from sound and using space symbolically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating her films, look for intentional non-realism: asynchronous sound-image relations, symbolic staging of space, and emphasis on verbal text within the film. Examples cited: her provocative cinema (1973–1983) and India Song; assess how these techniques create an 'ideal' image rather than documentary realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single 'ideal' image / balance of vacancy and meaning in cinema
rubrics_metrics.description: Duras' provocative cinema ... was concerned with a single 'ideal' image, at the same time both 'an absolute vacant image and an absolute meaningful image,' while also focused on the verbal text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate films for a haunting central visual/aural image that functions both as emptiness and meaning. Consider critical commentary (Cottenet-Hage and Kolker) about how this aesthetic shapes narrative and viewer response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic focus on love, sex, and human sexuality
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of her works ... deal with human sexuality. She explored love and sex across novels and films.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess recurrence and treatment of eroticism, desire, and sexual politics (e.g., L'Amant/The Lover, Le Ravissement de Lol V. Stein). Consider whether sexuality is central theme, means of psychological exploration, or disruptive force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of autobiographical material / fictionalized autobiography
rubrics_metrics.description: Her best-selling, highly fictionalized autobiographical work L'Amant (1984) ... The story of her adolescence also appears in three other books: The Sea Wall, Eden Cinema and The North China Lover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reading Duras, distinguish between factual life events and their fictionalized reworking; evaluate how autobiographical elements are transformed into fiction and what narrative purposes they serve (memory, confession, aesthetic distance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-genre and medium versatility
rubrics_metrics.description: Marguerite Duras was a novelist, playwright, screenwriter, essayist, and experimental filmmaker; author of many novels, plays, films, interviews, essays, and works of short fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess an author's oeuvre by range across genres and media, and how techniques migrate between them (e.g., theatrical dialogue informing prose, prose informing film scripts). Examples: script for Hiroshima mon amour, stage plays, directed films such as India Song.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical recognition and legacy as evaluative metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Her script for the film Hiroshima mon amour earned her a nomination for Best Original Screenplay at the Academy Awards; L'Amant won the Prix Goncourt; numerous other prizes and selections noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use awards, critical reception, adaptations, and influence (e.g., Beckett's reaction, film/TV depictions) as part of evaluation, while noting that recognition is only one axis of artistic value. Cite specific honors (Prix Goncourt, Academy Award nomination) and later portrayals or critical studies when arguing significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from single-school classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Although associated with movements, she 'did not belong definitively to any one group.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate Duras by her idiosyncratic blend of influences rather than forcing her into a single critical category. Look for hybrid techniques and personal aesthetics that resist neat labeling; avoid over-reliance on movement-based interpretation.
